title: The Opium Wars
key_facts: Two mid-19th century conflicts between Qing China and Western powers led by Britain
Centered on disputes over opium trade, diplomatic immunity, and treaty-port access
Resulted in unequal treaties reshaping China's foreign relations
causes: British opium imports into China and Chinese efforts to suppress the trade
Conflicts over sovereignty, extraterritoriality, and tariff control
outcome: Opening of treaty ports and cession of territory (e.g., Hong Kong after the First Opium War)
Expansion of foreign privileges and missionary access

figures.name: Lin Zexu
figures.role: Qing official who led opium suppression

figures.name: Charles Elliot
figures.role: British superintendent of trade in China

impacts: Weakened Qing sovereignty and accelerated internal crises
Expansion of Western commercial and diplomatic presence in China
Prelude to later reforms and upheavals in late Qing China
